knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A coarse scratch left under a fine grit shows through the finish. The sequence is followed so the surface is consistent.
A burn mark usually means the machine dwelt in one place. Sanding harder makes it deeper, so the machine and technique are checked first.
Fixings, the floor type and the completed pre-start assessment are checked before the first pass.
Raking light shows dips, swirl marks, burns and missed areas that are hard to see under overhead light.
The approved damp or HEPA method is used between grits. Dry sweeping and compressed air are not used.

practicalCriteria: Candidate completes the pre-start checks: assessment complete, protection in place, extraction connected and fixings checked.
Candidate sands a sample area through the manufacturer's grit sequence without skipping a grit.
Candidate inspects under raking light after each stage and marks any defect for correction.
Candidate records the grit sequence, the areas covered and the dust control used.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is separate. A knowledge pass does not establish practical competence, and the practical criteria must be observed and recorded by an assessor. Grit numbers are taken from the manufacturer for the job, not from this assessment.
evidenceRequired: Sanding record with grit sequence and areas
Raking light inspection record at each stage
Assessor observation of the sanding sequence
stopWorkCriteria: Sanding started before the pre-start assessment is complete
Burn mark sanded over without finding the cause
Dry sweeping or compressed air used between grits
Sanding over fixings that have not been checked
